speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have a known history of tuberculosis or other chronic lung diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The combination of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and a chronic cough for six months is highly concerning for tuberculosis. Given your history of incarceration, is there a possibility you were exposed to someone with TB in prison, or did you have any skin lesions or ulcers during your sentence?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.
